source.title: Circuit-Tracer: A New Library for Finding Feature Circuits
source.authors: Michael P. Hanna; Mateusz Piotrowski; Jack W Lindsey; E. Ameisen

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neuron polysemanticity and presents feature-circuit methods, but does not test the claim versions about neuron poles, explanations, or neuron-based circuits.
record.gate_note: The paper reports two feature-intervention case studies. They use transcoder features and do not measure the neuron-pole audit or the explanation properties named by the claim versions; their outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: A software paper for transcoder feature circuits. Its two case studies intervene on transcoder features in Gemma-2 (2B), not on native neurons. It does not measure neuron pole shares, explanation predictivity, simulation scores, or whether native-neuron attribution graphs suffice. It only restates the standard view that neurons are polysemantic (citing Olah 2017 and Elhage 2022) as motivation, with no data of its own.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present circuit-tracer as an efficient, accessible library (models up to 14B) for finding, visualizing, annotating and intervening on transcoder feature circuits. They show it reproduces two results from Lindsey et al. (2025) on Gemma-2 (2B). They note limitations: attention-related features are missed, error nodes can be uninterpretable, and annotation is manual.
record.recipe_differences: The paper implements transcoder feature circuits and interventions, not an audit of neuron poles or explanations of individual model neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The Dallas case restricts interventions to layers 16–21. The language case intervenes at non-BOS positions during open-ended generation.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2 (2B) with 2.5M-feature CLTs, intervening on Texas and California transcoder features (layers 16–21) shifts the top output from Austin (0.441) to Sacramento (0.303).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervening on selected transcoder features shifts a model's next-token prediction in a two-hop geography prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2 (2B) with GemmaScope PLTs, setting Spanish features to -2 times their original value changes the continuation from Spanish to English.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating language-related transcoder features changes the language of generated text.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The paper presents two brief case studies rather than a systematic evaluation. Feature labeling is manual, and the interventions do not establish the quality of neuron-level explanations or the sufficiency of native neurons as circuit units.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B neuron pole audit.
All: no neuron interpretability shares across models or scales.
All: InceptionV1 cat-car neuron is not examined; polysemanticity is only asserted from citations.
All: no measure of how interpretable neuron shares vary with tools or architecture.
All: graphs use trained transcoders with error nodes; native neurons are not tested as units (thresholded-MLP-neuron attribution is listed only as future work).
All: no test of whether explanations predict neuron firing.
All: no simulation scoring of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The only connection to the claim is the background statement that neurons are polysemantic, made without new evidence. This is the opposite of the essay's position but untested here, so the relation is discusses (T6).

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole audit and the stated shares of single-job, two-job, and not-yet-understood poles.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales up to trillions of parameters.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
The causes of late-layer messiness and the stated estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Whether attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations that fit activating examples predict where neurons fire on other activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text and the share receiving good scores.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (2B)
rows.operation_detail: Constrained feature intervention: the paper says Texas-feature activations were multiplied by 4 and California features were set to 10 times their original value at the Dallas position.

conditions.value: Fact: The capital of the state containing Dallas is
Texas features multiplied by 4; California features set to 10 times their original value

rows.note: The text says the top output changes from Austin to Sacramento. The accompanying plot shows pre-intervention Austin 0.441 and post-intervention Sacramento 0.303. The paper describes the intervention as downweighting Texas features, although it states the multiplier as 4.
rows.check: Measures a transcoder-feature intervention effect, not anything a version names. State 'observed' is relative to the paper's own intervention, not a claim version. Values are readable from Figure 3: Austin 0.441 before; Sacramento 0.303 after. Note the text says 'downweighting' while stating a multiplier of 4, likely meaning -4.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (2B)
rows.operation_detail: Open-ended generation intervention setting Spanish-feature activations to -2 times their original value at all non-BOS positions.

conditions.value: Spanish features set to -2 times their original value

rows.baseline: The model normally continues in Spanish.
rows.value: The intervention causes the model to continue with English-language text.
rows.note: The intervention outcome is described in the text; sampled examples are shown in Figure 4.
rows.check: Measures a transcoder-feature ablation effect on output language. It does not bear on any version about native neurons or their explanations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
